interpretation.mechanism: Parallel interpretation can organize existing experimental data and literature into research candidates. Expert preference for selected reports does not establish the proposed biological mechanisms.
interpretation.conditions: Read the original v1 main-text PDF/XML: distributed-agent results, literature comparison, blinded expert review, Figures 1/2/4 and Discussion. GPT-Rosalind-5.5 used human-supplied data, shared prompts, coding tools and literature access; the original manuscript was withheld.
interpretation.counterexample: More detailed reports can leave experimental work and independent validation unchanged. The comparison is with selected single-agent reports, not a measured human-only research campaign.
interpretation.evidence: The 55 testable findings are a subset of 71 source-study findings: 48 matched/refined plus four partially recovered. Thirty experts assessed 60 selected reports. The 45/60 preference result is 20 report pairs with three judgments each, not 60 independent discoveries.
interpretation.limits: Preprint v1 was posted October 16; the developer article appeared October 21. Run dates are unstated in the main text. Human months-to-year effort is illustrative, and fixed model/prompt/tools do not establish matched total compute. Supplementary methods could not be retrieved; no supplemental-only claim or independent replication is adopted.
interpretation.mitigation: Retain human review, independent datasets and prospective experiments before accepting mechanisms or downstream benefits. Count verification time, cost and unsuccessful candidates when assessing productivity.
interpretation.readerContext: The bilingual paragraph introduces the existing mouse-brain data and distinguishes report quality from experimental confirmation. It explains what the 32-minute figure covers before readers can mistake it for total research time.
interpretation.whyHere: Add bounded research assistance at R1 while preserving observed status. Do not upgrade R2, R3, R4, ASI or biological-misuse nodes from this result; neither recursive improvement nor broad dangerous capability was tested.

primary.locator: Main-text Results and Figures 1, 2, 4; Discussion; publisher version metadata
primary.support: Existing-data interpretation, report comparisons, exact denominators and remaining validation limits.

response.mechanism: Detection can fail to prevent harm when escalation or response is delayed. A proposed audit helps specify what to test without establishing a measured protection rate.
response.conditions: Read METR’s original proposal, especially the response section and access qualifications. It proposes authorized assessment of operational records and response, without a new model trial or measured stopping-time distribution.
response.counterexample: A warning may lead to timely containment, while permission limits or blocking may prevent an action before human review. A vulnerability in one layer does not establish irreversible harm.
response.evidence: Add the original methodological proposal as argument at C3b. Preserve limited status and the indirect evidence summary based on previously recorded incidents; the proposal is not an additional observed failure.
response.limits: A procedure is not a deployed mitigation or independent validation of a particular developer. Records, access and evaluator independence constrain the conclusion. Do not treat suggested sample sizes as completed experiments.
response.mitigation: Use response evidence to test the existing countermeasure claims. This review adds no operational attack procedure and does not claim that detection alone proves prevention.
response.readerContext: Both languages explain why an alert is insufficient and explicitly call the addition a proposal, located under countermeasures rather than presenting it as a new incident.
response.whyHere: C3b separates late response from C3a missed detection. Keep the oversight OR branches, local failure L and persistent loss C4 distinct; retain the existing evidence date and source attribution.

primary.locator: Response, including human evasion; Access details; footnotes 3, 4, 7
primary.support: Proposed evaluation of response, access limits and independence qualifications.

dependencies.mechanism: R1-R2 requires improvements to a real development bottleneck without offsetting verification delays. The oversight graph distinguishes missed detection from late response, not successive compulsory steps.
dependencies.conditions: Read R1-R2, the acceleration/research-cycle/oversight graphs, acceleration route/story, C3b evidence, three research news contexts and C3 parent context in both languages. New source results are checked against these unchanged conditions.
dependencies.counterexample: Biology-report preference can improve while total AI-development time remains unchanged. A late alert can still be followed by recovery, and prevention can come from another layer.
dependencies.evidence: The new study and proposal support their local additions, not the entire connection or all downstream conditions. News examples retain their original sources and existing limitations.
dependencies.limits: Dependency reading is not a renewed scientific audit of every older reference. Preserve original edge/evidence dates, classifications, topology, UI and unrelated content.
dependencies.mitigation: Keep whole-process measurement, verification and prevention conditions explicit. Do not infer acceleration or catastrophe from a local metric or evaluation proposal.
dependencies.readerContext: Tour text introduces research tasks and the role of verification before feedback and practical consequences. Both language editions retain the difference between assistance, full development and recursive improvement.
dependencies.whyHere: The added node references change dependency fingerprints. Recheck their meaning while leaving unsupported downstream claims and dates unchanged.

primary.support: Further independent and prospective evaluation is needed; elapsed analysis time is not whole research time.
A methodological proposal does not quantify downstream prevention.

publication.mechanism: Dated provenance and a change history distinguish new observations from proposals and from the date of editorial review.
publication.conditions: Inspect all 19 daily starting URLs for October 8–22; deduplicate against draft head da919633. Confirm publisher version metadata and original reports rather than adopting search snippets.
publication.counterexample: An index visit, appointment announcement or unchanged version listing does not justify renewing a scientific confirmation date.
publication.evidence: Add two sources and two research cards. Advance only the substantively changed R1/C3b node dates, new source dates and map asOf; preserve all 41 previous history entries with translations by ID.
publication.limits: No independent replication was verified in the bounded search. Supplementary methods retrieval failed and prior weekly IMF retrieval gaps remain. This record does not claim exhaustive literature coverage or production publication.
publication.mitigation: Keep omissions and source limits in the accompanying record, validate dependency and bilingual gates, and retain the work as a draft for human review.
publication.readerContext: The new history entry states what was absent, what changed and why, in both languages. Source publication and check dates remain separate.
publication.whyHere: Cover inventory, history and map metadata without blanket date renewal. Continue the existing proposal; no merge or deployment is authorized by this heartbeat.
